blocks.content: Covers key historical, cultural, and political figures associated with Assam — a heavily biographical-fact area tested through direct name-to-contribution matching.

items: Lachit Borphukan — Ahom general who led the decisive victory at the Battle of Saraighat (1671) against the Mughals; commemorated nationally through the Lachit Borphukan National Defence Academy Award, given annually to the best cadet at the National Defence Academy.

Gopinath Bordoloi — freedom fighter and the first Chief Minister of Assam post-independence; played a crucial role in Assam's political integration with India during a sensitive period; posthumously awarded the Bharat Ratna (India's highest civilian honour) in 1999.

Bishnu Rabha — multi-talented freedom fighter, artist, and cultural figure, often referred to as 'Kalaguru' (master of the arts) for his wide-ranging contributions to Assamese art, music, and the independence movement.
Chilarai — a 16th-century Koch dynasty military commander/prince, celebrated for his military campaigns and strategic contributions during the Koch kingdom's expansion.

Srimanta Sankardev — 15th–16th century polymath (saint, scholar, playwright, social-religious reformer); founder of the neo-Vaishnavite movement and the Satra institution, with vast contributions across Assamese literature, music, and performing arts.

Jyoti Prasad Agarwala — a prominent figure in Assamese cinema, literature, and music, often referred to as the 'father of Assamese cinema' for his pioneering contributions, including directing early Assamese films.

Bhupen Hazarika — internationally acclaimed singer, lyricist, and filmmaker, widely regarded as one of the most influential cultural figures of Assam and the broader Northeast; recipient of numerous national honours including the Bharat Ratna (posthumously, 2019) and the Dadasaheb Phalke Award.

Lakshminath Bezbaroa — a foundational figure in modern Assamese literature, celebrated for his contributions to Assamese short stories, essays, and children's literature; often referred to by the honorific 'Rasaraj'.

Assam has produced notable figures across sports (including internationally recognized athletes and sportspersons in various disciplines) and other public fields — candidates should stay updated on recent national award recipients and notable achievers from Assam, as these are frequently tested in current-affairs-linked GK sections.

Numerous Assamese individuals have received Padma awards and other national honours across science, arts, literature, and public service — reviewing recent (last 2–3 years) Padma award lists for Assam-origin recipients is a high-value current-affairs preparation step.

cells:
Exam Tip

• Name-to-contribution matching is the dominant question format in this chapter — a compact personal reference table (name, era, key achievement, notable honour) pays off significantly.

• Bhupen Hazarika's Bharat Ratna (2019, posthumous) is a frequently tested current-affairs-adjacent fact given its relative recency.

• Distinguish carefully between similarly-themed figures — e.g., Bishnu Rabha ('Kalaguru') vs Jyoti Prasad Agarwala ('father of Assamese cinema') are often used as confusable distractor options in the same question.
